questions.prompt: What is gender rigidity in this law?
choices: A refusal to recognize any sex difference at all
Overidentifying with a narrow masculine or feminine script
A temporary preference for one style of clothing or behavior

explanation.gentle: The chapter is about one-sided identity, not about denying all difference.
explanation.direct: Greene's problem is rigid role performance that narrows the self.
explanation.competitive: The role becomes a costume that runs the system.

questions.prompt: Why does Greene use Caterina Sforza in this chapter?
choices: To show a real figure who breaks narrow gender coding
To argue that history had no gender roles at all
To prove that softness is always weakness

explanation.gentle: She anchors the law in visible human range.
explanation.direct: The case shows how small rigid expectations can be compared with an actual person.
explanation.competitive: The anchor makes shallow coding look cheap.

questions.prompt: What role do anima and animus play in the chapter?
choices: They are mystical ideas with no behavioral use
They name the disowned complementary traits that remain active in the psyche
They prove every person should act exactly the same

explanation.gentle: The terms matter because rejected traits do not simply disappear.
explanation.direct: Greene uses them as mechanism for disowned complementary capacities.
explanation.competitive: The exiled side stays live even after the brand rejects it.

questions.prompt: A manager keeps acting unnaturally hard because asking for help feels humiliating. Which reading best fits the chapter?
choices: The manager is showing mature authority
The manager may be using gender rigidity to defend a narrow script
The manager simply has higher standards than others

explanation.gentle: The warning sign is performative hardness that blocks useful range.
explanation.direct: Authority has become a script instead of a flexible capacity.
explanation.competitive: The costume is outranking the task.

questions.prompt: Which pattern best shows projection in this law?
choices: Someone feels unusual contempt for a trait they have made unacceptable in themselves
Someone reflects calmly on a trait they admire
Someone changes behavior after honest feedback

explanation.gentle: Projection often shows up as intense reactions to traits the self has rejected.
explanation.direct: What feels most irritating in another person may be a disowned part of the self.
explanation.competitive: The field gets attacked for carrying hidden inventory.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's distinction between integration and caricature?
choices: Integration erases difference, while caricature celebrates it
Integration widens range, while caricature narrows the self into a role
Integration avoids all conflict, while caricature seeks it

explanation.gentle: The chapter argues for fuller range, not sameness.
explanation.direct: Caricature performs a script; integration broadens capacity.
explanation.competitive: One widens the toolkit. The other defends the costume.

questions.prompt: Why can rigid identity make judgment worse?
choices: Because it narrows range and makes projection more likely
Because it removes all ambition
Because it forces everyone into the same personality

explanation.gentle: The narrower the script, the easier it is to overreact and misread others.
explanation.direct: Rigidity reduces flexibility and turns disowned traits into targets.
explanation.competitive: The role narrows the read and heats up the reactions.

questions.prompt: How does chapter 13 connect to chapter 12 on grandiosity?
choices: Both chapters show the self hardening around a defensive image
Chapter 13 rejects the idea that self-image matters
Chapter 13 proves success always destroys identity

explanation.gentle: Grandiosity and rigidity are different ways the self narrows itself.
explanation.direct: One hardens around inflated specialness; the other around a one-sided role.
explanation.competitive: Both are defensive valuations wearing different costumes.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter lead into aimlessness next?
choices: Because loosening rigid identity recovers range, but range still needs direction
Because identity does not affect purpose at all
Because projection always disappears instantly once noticed

explanation.gentle: The next question after recovered range is where to aim it.
explanation.direct: The chapter opens capacity, and the next law asks what that capacity should serve.
explanation.competitive: Freed toolkit is not yet strategy.

questions.prompt: Which plan best fits the law of gender rigidity?
choices: Defend the role more strongly whenever a complementary trait feels awkward
Identify the trait you have disowned, stop projecting it outward, and practice integrating it directly
Pretend all differences are meaningless so no one feels judged

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks for integration, not stronger role defense or vague flattening.
explanation.direct: The right move is to reclaim rejected traits rather than attack them in other people.
explanation.competitive: Bring the exiled asset back in-house instead of policing the field.
